tier_rationale: No intentional radiator: the manufacturer's own product page lists no wireless connectivity, and Fluke's FCC grantee record (T68) shows it files radio grants for its wireless multimeters and Bluetooth test-tool adapters (F233 'Wireless Multimeter', DMFBLE Bluetooth adapter, TTBLE BLE module) while holding none for the 87V. It is a 9V-battery handheld with an LCD and no logic beyond measurement.
the_unplug_test: There is no router for this device to notice. It is a 9V-battery multimeter: probes, a rotary dial, and a digital display with an analog bar graph. Nothing about it depends on Wi-Fi, an app, or a Fluke account, at any point from unboxing to the end of its lifetime warranty.

repairability.notes: Fluke sells the 87V under a lifetime warranty and authorized service centers stock parts; the meter is a long-service instrument by design, not a consumable.

sources.supports: Manufacturer product page: no Bluetooth/Wi-Fi/app/cloud mentioned anywhere; 9V battery power, ~400 hours typical battery life, standalone true-RMS measurement with no connectivity claims of any kind.

FCC grantee list for Fluke Corporation (grantee code T68): no grant found for model 87V or 87-V. Sibling control: the same grantee holds grants for wireless test/measurement products, including F233 'Wireless Multimeter RDX Project' (2010), DMFBLE 'Test & Measurement products' Bluetooth adapter (2014), PCFBLE Bluetooth test-and-measurement module (2014), and TTBLE BLE module (2023) — Fluke demonstrably files when a product has a radio, and the 87V has no matching grant.
Authorized reseller listing used only for current price and stock status ($472.69 sale, list $579.99, 128 in stock), not for any tier-relevant claim.

open_questions: Fluke also sells an 87V MAX variant and Bluetooth-equipped 279 FC / 373 FC-style clamp meters in the same catalog — confirm a buyer does not accidentally pick a connected sibling under a similar name.
notes: Fluke is a clean case of Rule 3 in the SCOUT playbook: a vendor that files FCC grants for some models (wireless multimeters, Bluetooth test-tool adapters) and not others, which makes the absence of a grant for the 87V meaningful rather than just unsearched.
